newsitem.title: PERU: Shell wants "golden alley" linking Peru gas blocks.
newsitem.headline: Shell wants "golden alley" linking Peru gas blocks.

text.p: Royal Dutch/Shell said it plans to invest $22 million in exploring a new gas field, hoping to create a "golden alley" to link the recently-granted concession and its Camisea reserves.

In March, the government granted a concession to a consortium of oil firms made up of Shell and Mobil to explore Block 75 that slots between the two areas -- Block 88A and Block 88B -- of the Camisea fields in the eastern jungle.
"The idea is to build a 'golden alley' with Block 75," Shell Prospecting and Development (Peru) B.V. spokesman Andrew Vickers told Reuters at Nuevo Mundo -- the supply base for the Camisea project.

Exploration drilling should start in the new block next year after results have been collected from three appraisal wells in the Camisea fields, Alan Hunt, the company's managing director in Peru, said.
"We know it (Block 75) is there. We know it's got gas. But we don't know how much it has got and what quality it is," Vickers said in an interview conducted Wednesday.

At Camisea, Shell, which is the operating partner in a joint project with Mobil, knows it has huge reserves - - estimated to hold 11 trillion cubic feet of natural gas and 600 million barrels of natural gas liquids.
The company's $11 million investment -- including a $3 million airstrip -- at Nuevo Mundo has provided infrastructure that could also be used for its operations at Block 75, Hunt said.
